tip: Chwe (six) triggers aspirate mutation, so cant becomes chant, as in Chwe chant (six hundred).
Sawl (how many) always takes a singular noun, so it is sawl plentyn (how many children), never a plural.
Gyda triggers aspirate mutation, so pob becomes phob in Gyda phob parch (with all respect).
ymdrech is feminine, so a following adjective soft-mutates: bach becomes fach in ymdrech fach (small effort).
ar triggers soft mutation, so dydd becomes ddydd: ar ddydd Sadwrn (on Saturday).
Bydd is the future of bod (to be): Bydd y tywydd yn heulog means the weather will be sunny.
Paid a plus a verb is the singular way to say 'don't': Paid ag anghofio (don't forget).
The linking yn softens a following adjective, so cynnar becomes gynnar: di'n gynnar (you finish early).
Hyd y gwn i is a set phrase for 'as far as I know'; gwn is 'I know' from gwybod.
dadl is feminine, so it soft-mutates after the article: mae'r ddadl (the debate).
Possession uses mae gan, and the thing owned soft-mutates: ci becomes gi in Mae gan Eluned gi (Eluned has a dog).
The object of a short-form verb soft-mutates, so papur becomes bapur: Prynodd Rhodri bapur (Rhodri bought a paper).
ei meaning 'her' triggers aspirate mutation, so pen-blwydd becomes phen-blwydd: ei phen-blwydd (her birthday).
cystal is the equative of da (good), meaning 'as good as': cystal ag unrhyw gaws (as good as any cheese).
Roedd plus wedi makes the pluperfect: Roedd hi wedi ymarfer means she had practised.
fel na plus fyddai means 'so that ... would not': fel na fyddai'r defaid yn dianc (so the sheep would not escape).
erbyn marks a deadline, meaning 'by' a point in time: erbyn 2050 (by 2050).
